items.english: Nancy Lee was the 'whistling' Taki's dead father had taught them. His father used to say he had picked it up from the sailors there when, back in his schooldays in America, he had used the summer holidays to ship aboard a whaler. He used to say the sailors working on deck would fall to humming Nancy Lee at the least thing. Having taken to the whaler so badly that he had once thrown everything aside to work as one of its sailors, the father, when talk turned to the sea, in his pride and absorption loved to repeat his reminiscences with bold gestures, making the 'boat-song' Nancy Lee his refrain.
notes: Kept hearsay colouring with 'used to say' twice, as text repeats with だと云った; kept 'boat-song' with Nancy Lee to show ruby gloss.

items.english: Taki was taken, beyond its simple cheerfulness, with the strain in which a peculiar, faintly lingering sweet-and-bitter plaint seemed to drift, and even now it survived as his habit whenever he whistled. Apart from that he had almost nothing he could whistle.

She, on the grounds that its pathos was sickly-sweet to the point of blatancy and that the passages like a shouted chorus were forced, and out of a contrary taste that held an American sailors' song old and vulgar, claimed Taki's unconscious whistling got on her nerves and would cover her ears. Hauling in the rigging, taking the helm, racing up the mast — the accompanying tune, the 'chorus' cried out involuntarily to match arms hauling the rope with unsparing strength, if hummed by a comfortable sober face at ease, would no doubt look blatantly forced — but what lies in the breast of one working in the very middle of the ocean... a thing like that his wife, born in the capital and brought up only in the capital, once a delinquent girl, could not begin to imagine, not even in a dream.
notes: Em dashes kept only where Japanese has them. Rendered 不良少女あがり literally as 'once a delinquent girl' rather than softening; the evenness of the slight is part of the narration.

data.say: Drafted the Nancy Lee origin passage keeping hearsay, song title, and three registers level.
